perspective:
Keith’s available information:

- Keith knows Elizabeth as his colleague at the construction company: he is a construction worker and she is the receptionist. They have a friendly, professional relationship through his office visits for paperwork and project updates.
- Over the past few days, Keith observed Elizabeth being unusually curt/short with him. He believed she might be upset with him, possibly because of a misunderstanding or an unknown mistake he made.
- Keith asked Elizabeth whether he had upset her. He heard her say no, that she was dealing with personal stuff, and she apologized if she seemed short.
- Keith felt sympathetic. He told Elizabeth he understood she was going through a tough time, offered to be someone she could talk to, and suggested a coffee break. He heard her accept and thank him.
- During the coffee break, Elizabeth shared more about her stresses. Keith perceived them as quite severe. He thought professional help might benefit her but worried about offending her.
- Keith suggested Elizabeth consider talking to a professional, saying an external perspective can sometimes help. He heard her say she had thought about it but was unsure and hesitant.
- Keith noticed Elizabeth become slightly withdrawn after that. He believed his suggestion might have embarrassed her and felt regretful.
- Keith told Elizabeth he hoped he had not overstepped, and that he wanted her to know he was there to support her no matter what. He heard her say he did not overstep, she appreciated his concern, and it was a lot to think about.
- After their last conversation, Keith observed Elizabeth seeming more open and appreciative. He believed she valued his support and felt more comfortable around him. He intended to maintain this supportive relationship.
- Keith told Elizabeth he was glad they could talk and that he is always available if she needs to chat or take a break together. He heard her thank him, say it meant a lot, and say she felt better knowing she had his support.
